programs.name: USDA Section 504 Home Repair Grant
programs.description: Grant for very-low-income homeowners age 62 or older in USDA-eligible rural areas, to remove health and safety hazards.
programs.benefit_summary: Up to $10,000 lifetime grant ($15,000 in a presidentially declared disaster area). Can be combined with the 504 loan for up to $50,000.
programs.strings_attached: Repaid if the home is sold within 3 years. The homeowner must be unable to get affordable credit elsewhere.
programs.how_to_apply: Call the USDA Rural Development office for the county. Ask for Form RD 3550-35 (intake) and RD 3550-1 (authorization to release information).
programs.call_script: I'm calling for a homeowner age {age} in {county} County who owns and lives in the home. They have {repair} and can't afford the repair. Can you confirm the address is USDA-eligible and send the Section 504 grant intake form?
programs.status_note: Applications accepted year-round; approval time depends on local funding.

programs.name: USDA Section 504 Home Repair Loan
programs.description: 1% fixed-rate repair loan for low- and very-low-income homeowners in USDA-eligible rural areas who cannot get affordable credit elsewhere.
programs.benefit_summary: Up to $40,000 at 1% fixed for 20 years. Can be combined with the 504 grant for up to $50,000.
programs.strings_attached: This is a loan with monthly payments. Full title service is required if 504 loans total more than $25,000.
programs.how_to_apply: Call the USDA Rural Development office for the county; the same intake covers the grant and the loan.

programs.name: VA Home Improvements and Structural Alterations (HISA)
programs.description: Medically necessary access changes to a veteran's home: entry ramps, bathroom access, lowered counters and sinks.
programs.benefit_summary: Lifetime benefit of $6,800 for a service-connected condition or a 50%+ rating; $2,000 otherwise.
programs.strings_attached: Does not pay for roofs, furnaces, air conditioning or routine repairs. Needs a VA physician's prescription.
programs.how_to_apply: Ask the veteran's VA doctor for a prescription, then submit VA Form 10-0103 with an itemized estimate and a photo of the area to the Prosthetic and Sensory Aids Service.
programs.call_script: I'm helping a veteran who needs help with {repair} at home to get in and out safely. How do we get a HISA prescription and submit Form 10-0103?
programs.status_note: Lifetime benefit; ask PSAS how much of it the veteran has already used.

contacts.label: Prosthetic and Sensory Aids Service at the veteran's VA medical center
contacts.notes: Use the facility locator for the veteran's VA medical center.

programs.name: VA Specially Adapted Housing and Special Home Adaptation grants
programs.description: Grants to adapt a home for veterans with specific severe service-connected disabilities.
programs.benefit_summary: Up to $126,526 (SAH) or $25,350 (SHA) at fiscal 2026 rates; usable up to six times.
programs.strings_attached: Only for specific disabilities, such as loss of use of limbs, blindness in both eyes, severe burns or certain respiratory injuries.
programs.how_to_apply: Apply online with VA Form 26-4555, by mail or in person.
programs.call_script: I'm helping a veteran with a service-connected disability who needs help with {repair}. Can you tell us whether their rating qualifies for a Specially Adapted Housing or Special Home Adaptation grant?
programs.status_note: Amounts are for fiscal 2026 (to September 30, 2026); check for fiscal 2027 figures.
